sections.h2: What a Clearwater seller should know first
sections.html:
You have three basic options in Clearwater: hire an agent, sell on your own, or accept a cash purchase. The right one depends on the condition of the house, your timetable and any mortgage or renter attached to it. Population was 114,364 in July 2025, down 2.5% from the April 2020 estimate base, so local demand is not growing.

Roughly 24.1% of residents are 65 or older, so downsizing and estate sales account for a fair amount of the activity. Those sellers often prefer an as-is deal to a round of repairs.

A typical owner-occupied Clearwater home was valued at $361,300 for 2020 through 2024, and just 58.6% of housing is lived in by its owner. The rest is rental housing, which is why plenty of sellers in town are landlords with tenants still living in the house.

The gap between $1,908 and $811 suggests many owners have paid off their loans and sell with a large share of equity.

Yes, a landlord can sell. The city's Planning and Development Department publishes a Business Tax Receipt application for residential rentals, and it spells out what Clearwater expects of a rental. The form treats stays of under 31 days, or one calendar month if that is less, as outside a residential use in a residential zoning district.

If you rent by the night, read that wording before you list, because a buyer planning short stays will ask. The form also names the housing code items an inspector can review:

  • Kitchen sink, stove and refrigerator, plus bath fixtures and hot and cold water.
  • Heating, smoke detectors and fire protection.
  • Windows, ventilation and lighting in halls and stairways.
  • Electrical outlets and lights.
  • Walls, roofs, ceilings and floors, checked for leaks.
  • Stairs, porches, doors, and pest control.

It also requires a local property manager with a street address in Pinellas, Hillsborough, Pasco, Manatee or Sarasota County. Before a rental changes hands, ask Planning and Development about the current fee and the registration steps for the new owner.

The same application lists exterior standards that code officers apply to any residential lot: abandoned vehicles, address numbers, debris, sound fences, graffiti, overgrown grass, outdoor storage, parking, lighting and trash facilities.

Walk the lot with that list before the first showing. A boat on the grass or a tall lawn can draw a complaint mid-sale, and a buyer's inspector will note the same things. Fixing them costs little next to a price cut, and a clean exterior also makes a stronger first impression in photos and drive-bys.

sections.h2: Value and exemptions at the Pinellas County Property Appraiser
sections.html:
The county property appraiser sets values. Visit the main office at 315 Court Street, 2nd floor, Clearwater, weekdays from 8 AM to 5 PM. Condos and manufactured homes come with their own paperwork, so ask the office which forms fit your property type.

Values are set as of January 1. Exemption applications close March 1, and a TRIM notice with proposed values comes in August. A sale counts as a change of ownership, so the next January 1 the home is revalued at full just value.

sections.h2: Deed tax and tax bills at closing
sections.html:
State tax on a Pinellas deed is 70 cents per $100 of price. The statute makes every signer answerable regardless of who the contract says pays. The clerk collects at recording. Look for that line on your settlement sheet before you sign.

Tax bills are mailed in November. The discount is 4 percent for November payment and falls a point each month to 1 percent in February. Unpaid bills are delinquent from April 1. A closing in mid-year means the title company shares the bill with the buyer. Ask how it plans to divide it.

sections.h2: What if a Clearwater owner is behind on the mortgage?
sections.html:
Foreclosure in Florida goes through a judge. After final judgment the clerk sets an auction between 20 and 35 days out, or later if the lender agrees, and the winner leaves a 5 percent deposit. A sale before the auction pays the lender from proceeds and may end the case.

The certificate of title that follows an auction triggers deed tax measured on the top bid. Call your loan servicer or a Florida attorney soon, and set a cash offer beside a short sale before an auction date arrives.

Settle who has authority first, because heirs cannot convey clean title on their own. Summary administration, a streamlined court process, is open to estates of $150,000 or less in non-exempt assets and to estates opened over two years after the death. If a will goes through probate, the representative's deed is listed by the state as free of deed tax.

Creditor claims are barred unless filed within three months of first publication of the notice, or 30 days after a creditor is served, whichever is later. For deaths after 2004 there is no Florida estate tax. The probate court clerk can say which path applies to this estate.

Even a quick sale goes better when the house presents cleanly. Clear counters and closets, trim overgrown plants, and fix small leaks and loose fixtures. If an inspector will be walking through, make sure attic and utility areas are reachable. Tell buyers about known defects rather than hoping they miss them, because a late surprise is the most common reason an agreed price gets reopened. Keep your receipts and any warranty papers together so you can hand them over at closing. If the house is rented, give the tenant plenty of warning before any showing, and be courteous, since a cooperative tenant makes the whole sale smoother.

sections.h2: A simple plan for a fast Clearwater sale
sections.html: Pick the route first, then work backward from the closing date. Collect your deed, newest tax bill and lender payoff letters. Inspect the yard for exterior problems, and have the city check your address for open permits or violations. With tenants in place, add the lease, deposit record and rent ledger. Request written offers with proof of funds, and compare the net after fees and repairs. Choose a closing date you can truly meet. A few days ahead of signing, get a draft settlement statement from the title company.

faqs.q: Is a cash sale in Clearwater faster than listing?
faqs.a: Closing can come within days or weeks, since no lender or appraisal stands in the way. A listing adds showings, repair negotiations and loan timelines. Estimate your net on each path first.

faqs.q: Does Clearwater require a permit or inspection to sell?
faqs.a: No city permit is required merely to sell. Open permits and code violations can still hold up a closing, so ask Planning and Development to check your address.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Clearwater house with tenants?
faqs.a: Yes. A sale does not cancel the lease by itself. Unpaid rent calls for 3 days' written notice, and ending a month-to-month tenancy takes 30 days, so the buyer either keeps the tenant or waits out proper notice.

faqs.q: Who pays deed tax on a Clearwater sale?
faqs.a: The state can pursue any signer, and contracts usually put the cost on the seller. The state rate is 70 cents per $100.

faqs.q: Where do I check my Clearwater homestead status?
faqs.a: Ask the Pinellas County Property Appraiser. New filings are due March 1. Renting the home, or no longer living in it, ends the homestead.
